subject: Top-up latch proposal — invoice split + annual credit

Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Top-up latch proposal — invoice split + annual credit

Hi Anna / Procurement team,

Following our call this morning, attached is a concise proposal for handling the mid-contract additional capacity you expect in Q4. The core idea is a latching top-up that avoids immediate full-rate retentions while preserving predictable renewal economics:

- What we heard: you need to absorb an expected surge this quarter (approx. +30% token volume) but prefer to avoid a full midterm reprice and multiple invoices.
- Proposed mechanism (short): Redwood invoices 50% of the incremental top-up at time of purchase (covers immediate capacity), and we apply the remaining 50% as a credit against next annual renewal (co-term). This preserves your cashflow preference and gives you a guaranteed renewal credit.
- Surge cap / latch: credits only apply up to a pre-agreed surge threshold (example: 40% over baseline). Usage beyond the threshold would be treated as overage and invoiced monthly.
- Operational notes: we can execute via a one-page amendment (SOW addendum) and a lightweight DocuSign; billing needs PO as usual.

Attachments: rwd_topup_latch_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal), cost_table_options.csv (three invoice/credit permutations).

If this matches what you discussed with your finance team, we can send a formal amendment and the DocuSign link today.

Thanks,
Irene

Anna — quick answers and two concrete options so you can pick what works for procurement: 

Option A — Immediate prorated invoice (standard)
- Redwood invoices full cost of top-up prorated to co-term at purchase.
- Net-30. No renewal credit; renewal reflects updated committed units.
- Pros: accounting simplicity, immediate revenue recognition.
- Cons: you pay full cash up-front.

Option B — 50/50 Invoice + Renewal Credit (our proposed latch)
- Invoice 50% of top-up at purchase (Net-30); remaining 50% recorded as a pre-paid credit applied at next annual renewal invoice.
- Credit appears as a negative line item on renewal invoice and on the renewal statement (we'll include reference to PO/AMENDMENT).
- Surge latch: credit capped at X% (we used 40% example in the attached CSV). Anything above the cap billed as overage monthly.
- Pros: reduces near-term cash hit for you, preserves renewal economics.
- Cons: partial deferral of Redwood revenue to renewal.

Operationally we can provision once we have a PO referencing the amendment. Legal team has signoff to proceed with a one-page addendum; DocuSign link will follow. Attached is a quick calculator (cost_table_options.csv) with figures for both options at your baseline and at +30%/ +50% usage.

If procurement is comfortable with Option B, I recommend we prepare the amendment and DocuSign today and provision capacity once PO comes through.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Success (Growth) — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Top-up latch proposal — invoice split + annual credit

Anna — Kimberly from Finance here. A few notes from the billing/legal side and a suggested compromise if procurement wants stronger cash alignment: 

- We can accept a PO referencing the addendum and provision capacity upon receipt of PO. Standard practice is to require the signed amendment for contract completeness, but we can operationally provision with PO + signed order form.
- For the 50% invoice: Net-30 is fine. The renewal credit will show as a single negative line item on the renewal invoice with a cross-reference to the original invoice and PO.
- Compromise option (if procurement wants less deferred revenue exposure): invoice 60% at purchase and apply 40% at renewal as a credit. This reduces Redwood deferment while still softening your near-term cash hit.

DocuSign: I'll prepare the addendum with the selectable credit cap (we'll populate the exact percent you choose) and send the link. We also need a PO number for SSO of billing; happy to accept a preliminary PO and update final PO on signature.

Atts: rwd_topup_latch_proposal_v1.pdf (amendment summary).

Best,
